I was about to file a duplicate, but this issue already covers the root behavior. Adding a Linux + `oh-my-opencode-slim@latest` repro because it reproduced the same stale `@latest` cache path after `opencode plugin -g -f`.

### Repro

- Published latest observed:

  ```sh
  pnpm view oh-my-opencode-slim version
  # 2.0.0
  ```

- Cached plugin version observed before workaround:

  ```text
  OpenCode plugin cache entry for oh-my-opencode-slim@latest reported: 1.1.2
  ```

- Force-updating global plugin config:

  ```sh
  opencode plugin -g -f oh-my-opencode-slim@latest
  ```

  This updated the OpenCode plugin config, but the cached plugin still reported `1.1.2`. The UI kept loading the old version until the cache directory was removed.

### Workaround

```sh
rm -rf <OpenCode plugin cache dir>/packages/oh-my-opencode-slim@latest
opencode plugin -g -f oh-my-opencode-slim@latest
```

After removing the cache directory, `@latest` resolved to `2.0.0`.

### Suggested fix direction

The cache key appears to be the literal spec string, so `oh-my-opencode-slim@latest` reuses the same cache entry even when npm `latest` changes. A robust fix would resolve floating specs before cache lookup and include the resolved version in the cache key, or force-delete/refresh the existing cache directory when `-f` is used with a floating spec.

Example direction:

```ts
async function installPlugin(spec: string, options: { force?: boolean }) {
  const resolved = await resolvePackageSpec(spec);
  // Example: oh-my-opencode-slim@latest -> oh-my-opencode-slim@2.0.0
  const cacheKey = `${resolved.name}@${resolved.version}`;
  const cacheDir = getPluginCacheDir(cacheKey);

  if (options.force) {
    await fs.rm(cacheDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }

  await ensurePluginCache(cacheDir, resolved.spec);
}
```

### Template fields

- OpenCode version: `1.17.4`
- Terminal: `xterm-256color`
- Operating System: Linux/WSL
- Screenshot/share link: not attached; reproduced via CLI/cache inspection instead.

## Update (`dbbe67f066fe`)

13 items are now resolved (mostly via SDK v1.29.0), 5 are partially resolved, and the rest confirmed still missing.

### Resolved

- Pagination is fully implemented — generic `paginate()` with cursors, cycle detection, 1000-page cap
- Most auth/transport items (token refresh, RFC 8707/9728, OIDC, step-up, session-id, reconnect, Last-Event-ID) are handled by the SDK now
- `structuredContent` and `resource_link` are handled
- `headers` config is now sent in `mcp auth`/`mcp debug`
- Cancellation IS working — `signal: options.abortSignal` is passed through, SDK sends `notifications/cancelled` on abort

### Still missing

- Core capabilities: sampling, elicitation, roots, subscriptions, templates, completion, ping, tasks — all still completely missing
- No `capabilities` object at initialize
- `InitializeResult.instructions` not captured
- Progress: `onprogress` callback never wired to `callTool`, so no progressToken sent and no events surfaced
- `isError` not checked, `audio` dropped, tool annotations ignored
- OAuth callback server leak + XSS still present
- Security mitigations (Origin validation, SSRF) not implemented
- `mcp debug` still hardcodes protocol version `2024-11-05`
- No per-agent MCP tool filtering (model tool limits)

### Clean up

Removed 56 resolved closed issues/PRs from the related list. Re-added 17 that were closed but never actually implemented (sampling, elicitation, roots, instructions, resource subscriptions, progress).

We ran into this too. In our reference implementation (proposal #32166, PR #32167) the depth-3 silent failure is gone: the root cause on our side was `task_id` resume targeting a non-direct-child session, which produced an unparented/silent run. Resume is now restricted to direct children, and over-depth spawns fail loudly with a typed `SubagentDepthError` instead of dying silently — chains of 3+ levels (up to 5) work and are covered by tests.

This is addressed in PR #32167 (proposal #32166). Permission asks raised anywhere in a nested tree are now routed to the **root** session (carrying `originSessionID`/`originAgent`/`originDepth` metadata), and the headless `run` loop's permission filter was made tree-aware — so an ask from a grandchild no longer hangs forever. There's a regression test for the root-routing case.

Re: not being able to see the progress of sub-agents spawned by sub-agents — PR #32167 (proposal #32166) adds a TUI tree view with depth badges and an "asked by @agent (depth N)" indicator so nested sub-agent activity is visible. Would be glad to align it with whatever the team prefers here.

We built something close to this: a deterministic multi-agent workflow layer (fan-out / pipeline / synthesize across ephemeral sub-agent sessions, with per-agent worktree isolation and an abort cascade) on top of nested sub-agent spawning. Reference implementation in PR #32167, design-review proposal in #32166 — curious whether it overlaps with the ephemeral-teams approach you had in mind.
